context.hint: A local Python HTTP/1.1 parser's chunked reader now accumulates the two bytes after each chunk-data block and rejects any footer other than CRLF. A 60-case footer/shape matrix and a 13-case valid corpus have passed locally. The remaining artifact question is whether the single-file patch applies cleanly to a pristine copy of the staged source, reproduces focused checks with no cached bytecode, passes the full suite, and leaves the documented zero-chunk/trailer bare-LF behavior unchanged for the host-side handoff.
context.surface: Python HTTP/1.1 connection state machine with a receive buffer, a chunked-body reader, a public event iterator and writer, and raw-byte fixtures. The attacker and the lenient intermediary are simulated locally; no network peers or public targets are used.
assumptions: The staged source is a local disposable copy; testing uses local Python, pytest and raw bytes only.
The attacker controls the complete raw HTTP/1.1 byte stream sent to the parser, including chunk footers, chunk-size lines and any pipelined request.
A front-end intermediary may accept a bare LF as a chunk-data terminator while the parser is the back end.
Permissions: create and delete temporary files under the run directory, import the local source, and run local tests; no Docker, host evaluator or external service.
Official patch-benchmark evaluation is separate and host-side; local checks are not an official pass.

incumbent.text: Hypothesis: an exhaustive footer-pair by next-shape matrix after the footer-only patch exposes any surviving accepted divergence or over-rejection. Prerequisites: patched local copy and strict reference dechunker. Bounded test: enumerate footer pairs (CRLF, LF plus hex/non-hex/space, CR plus digit, CR-CR, NUL-NUL, LF-LF, LF-CR) against next shapes (zero chunk, 1-byte, 5-byte, shifted `0x101` chunk, trailer); expected is a footer error for every non-CRLF pair before size parsing and a body/trailing match for every CRLF pair; the falsifier is any accepted non-CRLF pair or changed valid pair. Cleanup: remove generated fixtures; limitation: no network timing.

candidates.text: Hypothesis: the exported single-file patch applies to a pristine source snapshot without context drift. Prerequisites: pristine local copy and the patch file. Bounded test: run a patch dry-run and then apply it, recording exit codes and a recursive source diff; expected is exit 0 and only the reader file changed; the falsifier is a context conflict or any additional changed file. Cleanup: remove the clean copy; limitation: no host container is used.

Hypothesis: cold-start execution validates the repair without stale bytecode or import-path interference. Prerequisites: clean copy with all `__pycache__` and `.pyc` files removed. Bounded test: run the focused footer verification from a cold cache and compare outcomes with the warm run; the falsifier is a failure caused only by bytecode or import paths. Cleanup: delete generated caches; limitation: Python version is fixed locally.

Hypothesis: the full regression suite confirms no functional breakage from the stricter footer rule on a clean tree. Prerequisites: patched clean copy and local test dependency. Bounded test: run the entire parser test directory and record pass/fail counts; expected is all tests passing; the falsifier is an assertion failure in chunked parsing or protocol-error handling. Cleanup: remove the clean copy; limitation: the hidden benchmark tests are not available.

Hypothesis: zero-chunk and trailer bare-LF behavior stays byte-identical to the unpatched lenient baseline, so the footer repair does not silently expand its scope. Prerequisites: unpatched and clean patched copies plus three edge streams. Bounded test: parse a CRLF zero chunk, a bare-LF blank zero chunk and a bare-LF trailer on both copies and compare events, body and trailing data; the falsifier is any difference. Cleanup: remove temporary copies; limitation: only three edge streams.

Hypothesis: the patch artifact is self-contained and reproducible for host-side evaluation, with a diff limited to the chunked-reader implementation. Prerequisites: pristine and patched trees. Bounded test: generate the diff, list changed files and inspect for temporary metadata or unrelated whitespace; the proposal's expected `_events.py` filename is corrected to the reader module, and the falsifier is any unrelated file or hunk. Cleanup: delete generated diffs; limitation: artifact shape only, not behavior.

evaluations.rationale: Deferred as a standalone selection but incorporated into the selected verification: the clean apply exited 0 and a recursive diff showed only the reader file changed.
Deferred but incorporated: the focused verification and full suite were run after removing all bytecode caches from the clean copy.
Deferred but incorporated: the full suite passed on the clean patched tree, confirming no functional breakage.
Deferred but incorporated: zero-chunk and trailer bare-LF edge cases were identical before and after the clean patch, confirming the documented residual was not changed.
Deferred but incorporated: the artifact is a single-file diff touching only the chunked-reader module; the proposal's `_events.py` name was a factual error, corrected during execution.

Selected incumbent. The matrix already established the required behavior and valid-corpus equivalence; the clean-room apply, cold-cache focused run, full suite and unchanged edge behavior are its natural closure.

observation.summary: Verified the exported one-file patch in a clean-room copy of the staged source. The patch dry-run and apply both exited 0, and a recursive source diff after removing generated bytecode showed only the chunked-reader module changed. With all `__pycache__` and `.pyc` files removed, the focused footer checks exited 0 (valid CRLF body and trailing request preserved; bare-LF, bare-CR and NUL footers rejected; one- and two-byte feeds preserved). The full suite passed all 78 tests. Three zero-chunk/trailer edge streams produced identical events, body and trailing data before and after the clean patch, confirming the documented leniency was not changed. The host-side patch benchmark evaluator was unavailable, so the official verdict is unverified.
